newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty swings in nervous trade, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Zloty swings in nervous trade, seen stabilising.

text.p: The Polish zloty swung between 2.3 and 2.05 percent from the parity rate in nervous trade after a sudden foreign currency purchase made many players wonder if the central bank had been active, dealers said.

Dealers said a foreigner bought some $12 million after a stop loss sale of Polish T-bills and big players followed the trend to cover positions in case the initial zloty fall had been caused by a central bank intervention.
"After the zloty's recent deep fall a foreign client made a stop-loss sale of Polish treasuries which triggered a nervous market reaction," one dealer at a foreign bank here said.

At 1040 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.21/2.05 percent from the trading band centre against the opening's 2.36/2.27 percent. It was at 3.0180/3.0225 to the dollar, down from 3.0135/60 and at 1.8260/90 to the mark, down from 1.8230/50.
Dealers said zloty trade was likely to stabilise at around 2.10 percent from the parity rate as traders closed positions.
"I do not expect further zloty swings today," said Adam Roeske from Bank Gdanski.
At 1055 GMT O/N rates were at 21.70/85 percent, up from opening's 21.40/21.75 percent, T/N were also up at 21.75/21.90 percent from 21.40/21.75. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
